meta.titre: Mensuration: Perimeters, Areas, Surface Areas and Volumes
meta.sous_theme: Perimeter, area, surface area and volume of common shapes and solids

sections.contenu_markdown: A builder in Limbe has to fence a rectangular plot, tile a circular fountain and fill a cylindrical water tank for a school. Each job asks for a different measurement: the length of fence is a perimeter, the tiles cover an area, and the water fills a volume. Mensuration is the part of mathematics that measures lengths, areas and volumes, and it supplies several marks in every GCE Mathematics paper. The calculations are simple, but you earn marks only by choosing the right formula, using consistent units and writing the correct unit in the answer.

items: The area of a rectangle is length times width.
The radius of a circle is half of its diameter.

sections.titre: Formulae for perimeter, area, surface area and volume
sections.contenu_markdown:
**Plane shapes.** Perimeter is a length (cm, m); area is in square units (cm$^2$, m$^2$).

| Shape | Perimeter | Area |
|---|---|---|
| Rectangle ($l$, $w$) | $2(l + w)$ | $lw$ |
| Triangle (base $b$, height $h$) | sum of the sides | $\dfrac{1}{2}bh$ |
| Parallelogram | sum of the sides | base $\times$ height |
| Trapezium (parallel sides $a$, $b$, height $h$) | sum of the sides | $\dfrac{1}{2}(a + b)h$ |
| Circle (radius $r$) | $C = 2\pi r$ | $A = \pi r^2$ |

**Solids.** Volume is in cubic units (cm$^3$, m$^3$); surface area is in square units.

| Solid | Volume | Surface area |
|---|---|---|
| Cuboid ($l$, $w$, $h$) | $lwh$ | $2(lw + lh + wh)$ |
| Cube (side $a$) | $a^3$ | $6a^2$ |
| Cylinder ($r$, $h$) | $\pi r^2 h$ | curved $2\pi rh$; total $2\pi r(r + h)$ |
| Cone ($r$, height $h$, slant $l$) | $\dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$ | curved $\pi rl$; total $\pi r(r + l)$ |
| Sphere (radius $r$) | $\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$ | $4\pi r^2$ |
| Prism | area of cross-section $\times$ length | sum of all faces |

For a cone, $l^2 = r^2 + h^2$ (Pythagoras). Use the value of $\pi$ given in the question: usually $\dfrac{22}{7}$ or $3.14$.

**Units.** Convert all lengths to the same unit **before** calculating. $1\ \text{litre} = 1000\ \text{cm}^3$ and $1\ \text{m}^3 = 1000$ litres.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question gives a sector of a circle, with centre angle $\theta$ degrees.
variantes.contenu_markdown: A sector is a fraction $\dfrac{\theta}{360}$ of the whole circle. Arc length $= \dfrac{\theta}{360} \times 2\pi r$ and sector area $= \dfrac{\theta}{360} \times \pi r^2$. The perimeter of the sector is the arc length plus the two radii.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a solid is a container and the answer is wanted in litres, or a cost has to be found.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Find the volume in cm$^3$ or m$^3$, then convert: divide cm$^3$ by $1000$ to get litres, or multiply m$^3$ by $1000$. For costs, multiply the quantity (metres of fence, square metres of paint) by the price per unit.

sections.enonce_markdown:
A cylindrical water tank has an inside radius of $0.7$ m and a height of $2$ m. Take $\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$.

(a) Calculate the volume of the tank in cubic metres.

(b) Write the capacity in litres.

(c) How many 20-litre buckets can be filled from a full tank?

etapes.action: Write the formula for the volume of a cylinder.
etapes.justification: The tank is a cylinder, so $V = \pi r^2 h$.

etapes.action: Substitute the values with the same unit (metres).
etapes.justification: Both $r$ and $h$ are already in metres, so the volume will come out in m$^3$.
Divide $0.49$ by $7$ first to avoid a long decimal: $0.49 \div 7 = 0.07$.

etapes.action: Divide by the size of a bucket.
etapes.justification: Each bucket takes $20$ litres, so the number of buckets is the capacity divided by $20$.

sections.conclusion_markdown: (a) $V = 3.08\ \text{m}^3$. (b) The capacity is $3080$ litres. (c) $154$ buckets can be filled.

items.erreur_markdown: Using the diameter in $A = \pi r^2$: a circle of diameter $14$ cm has area $\dfrac{22}{7} \times 14^2 = 616\ \text{cm}^2$.
items.pourquoi_faux: The formula needs the **radius**, which is half the diameter. Using $14$ instead of $7$ makes the area four times too big.

items.erreur_markdown: Mixing units: a rectangle $2$ m by $50$ cm has area $2 \times 50 = 100$.
items.pourquoi_faux: The two lengths are in different units, so the product has no meaning. The unit is also missing.

items.erreur_markdown: Using the vertical height instead of the slant height in the curved surface area of a cone, $\pi r h$.
items.pourquoi_faux: The curved surface is made by the slant side of the cone, not the vertical height.
items.correction_markdown: Find $l = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2}$ first, then use $\pi r l$.

items.erreur_markdown: Forgetting the factor $\dfrac{1}{3}$ in the volume of a cone or pyramid.
items.pourquoi_faux: A cone fills exactly one third of the cylinder with the same base and height, so $\pi r^2 h$ is three times too big.

items.erreur_markdown: Giving an area in cm and a volume in cm$^2$.
items.pourquoi_faux: Area is measured in square units and volume in cubic units; a wrong unit loses the accuracy mark.
items.correction_markdown: Perimeter: cm. Area: cm$^2$. Volume: cm$^3$.

items.enonce_markdown: A rectangular plot is $25$ m long and $18$ m wide. Find its perimeter and its area. The plot is fenced at a cost of 1 500 FCFA per metre. Find the total cost of the fence.
items.solution_markdown:
Perimeter $= 2(25 + 18) = 2 \times 43 = $ **86 m**.

Area $= 25 \times 18 = $ **450 m$^2$**.

Cost of the fence $= 86 \times 1500 = $ **129 000 FCFA**.

items.enonce_markdown:
A circle has radius $14$ cm. Take $\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$.

(a) Find its circumference and its area.

(b) A sector of this circle has a centre angle of $90^\circ$. Find the length of its arc and its area.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $C = 2\pi r = 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 14 = $ **88 cm**. $A = \pi r^2 = \dfrac{22}{7} \times 14^2 = \dfrac{22}{7} \times 196 = $ **616 cm$^2$**.

(b) The sector is $\dfrac{90}{360} = \dfrac{1}{4}$ of the circle. Arc length $= \dfrac{1}{4} \times 88 = $ **22 cm**. Sector area $= \dfrac{1}{4} \times 616 = $ **154 cm$^2$**.

items.enonce_markdown:
A funnel is in the shape of a cone with base radius $9$ cm and vertical height $12$ cm. Take $\pi = 3.14$.

(a) Calculate the slant height.

(b) Calculate the curved surface area.

(c) Calculate the volume.

(d) Find the total surface area, including the circular base.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $l^2 = 9^2 + 12^2 = 81 + 144 = 225$, so $l = $ **15 cm**.

(b) Curved surface area $= \pi r l = 3.14 \times 9 \times 15 = 3.14 \times 135 = $ **423.9 cm$^2$**.

(c) $V = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \dfrac{1}{3} \times 3.14 \times 81 \times 12 = 3.14 \times 324 = $ **1017.36 cm$^3$**.

(d) The base area is $\pi r^2 = 3.14 \times 81 = 254.34$ cm$^2$. The total surface area is $423.9 + 254.34 = $ **678.24 cm$^2$**.

items_markdown: Perimeter is a length (cm, m); area is in square units (cm$^2$, m$^2$); volume is in cubic units (cm$^3$, m$^3$).
Circle: $C = 2\pi r$ and $A = \pi r^2$, using the **radius**; cylinder: $V = \pi r^2 h$; cone: $V = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$; sphere: $V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$.
A sector with angle $\theta$ is $\dfrac{\theta}{360}$ of the circle for both arc length and area.
For a cone, find the slant height with $l^2 = r^2 + h^2$ before using $\pi r l$.
Convert all lengths to one unit first; $1\ \text{m}^3 = 1000$ litres and $1\ \text{litre} = 1000\ \text{cm}^3$.
